children.text: Molo Mansion is a mansion completed in 1926 in Iloilo City's Molo district, standing across from Molo Plaza and Molo Church. It blends neoclassical and Art Deco elements and is now used for local souvenir shops, cafes and restaurants.

Molo Mansion is a historic house in the Molo district of Iloilo City. Its original name is the Lacson–Yusay Ancestral House, or the Yusay–Consing Ancestral House, and it is popularly called Molo Mansion. According to Wikipedia the building stands in front of Molo Plaza and Molo Church and has neoclassical lines with subtle Art Deco touches. Its coordinates are roughly 10.6965 N, 122.5434 E, about
3 km
east of central Iloilo City, in the Molo district.

The mansion was completed in 1926. It was built by Doña Petra Lacson of the Lacson clan and Estanislao Yulo Yusay, a prominent lawyer and judge from Molo, and the couple had ten children. After Estanislao died in 1940, their daughter Rosario Yusay inherited the house. Rosario's husband, Timoteo Consing Sr., served as governor of Iloilo from 1934 to 1937, and the house later passed to their son Timoteo Consing Jr. and his wife Nieva Ramirez-Consing. Nieva was one of the owners of Passi Sugar Central, a sugar mill that Universal Robina Corporation acquired in 2007.
The former mansion now houses shops selling Iloilo products and cafés. The
Kultura store directory
places its Molo Mansion shop on the ground floor on Locsin Street. See the façade from the plaza, then check the shops’ opening hours and which floors are accessible that day.

Molo, where the mansion stands, is one of Iloilo's oldest districts. It began in 1637 as a district for Chinese traders who supplied the nearby town of Villa de Arevalo (a Parián, or Chinatown), and in the 1800s it became a center of learning in the Visayas and earned the nickname Athens of the Philippines. On August 4, 1896, José Rizal is said to have passed through and exclaimed "La iglesia bonita!" on seeing the church, and on August 25, 1937 Molo was annexed to Iloilo City as a district. This guide covers the story of the mansion itself and also ties the plaza, the church and the food into a half-day route. For the best visit to the mansion, look first at the balance of the facade from the plaza, then go inside and look up at the ceiling and structure, and finish with a rest at a cafe.

The building is known for its high ceilings, neoclassical balustrades and finely carved decoration. If you study the columns, balustrade and window proportions of the facade slowly, you can sense the taste of a wealthy family of the time. Go inside during shop hours and look at the ceiling and staircase too.

The ownership history running from the Lacson family to the Yusay and Consing families involves lawyers, judges, a governor and the sugar industry. It is a small window onto Iloilo's sugar-cane economy and the prosperity of its leading families.

Inside are shops selling local specialties and food, such as Kultura, Sabor Ilonggo and Plantopia. It is a good place to look at hablon weaving, traditional sweets and local foods in one stop, and it is convenient for choosing gifts.
Cafes and restaurants offer coffee and snacks in the atmosphere of an old house. On a hot day it is a good place to rest in air-conditioned comfort and adjust your plans.

Counted as the most beautiful of the seven district plazas of Iloilo City, it has statues of Greek goddesses and a Maria Clara monument, and a fountain was added in a rehabilitation in August 2022. It is right in front of the mansion, so the two are easy to walk together.

blocks.title: The view across from Molo Church

children.text: Molo Church, with its striking red spires, stands across the plaza. It is also called the feminist church for the 16 statues of female saints on its pillars, and was declared a national landmark in 1992. You can frame the church in a single photo from in front of the mansion.

You can taste pancit Molo, a pork dumpling soup named after Molo, right here. Wonton-style wrappers are filled with ground pork and the soup is served with shredded chicken and shrimp. Rather than claim one place is best, compare bowls yourself around the plaza.

Iloilo has more heritage houses, including the Lacson Ruins, the Cesar Lacson Locsin Ancestral House, the Lopez Heritage House, the Ledesma Mansion and the Lizares Mansion. You can continue a walk through Iloilo's mansions with Molo Mansion as the starting point.
Arrive at Molo Plaza from central Iloilo by taxi, Grab or jeepney. Start by looking around the plaza's fountain and statues.
See the exterior and decoration from the front of Molo Mansion and take photos, then go inside and look around the souvenir shops.
Take a break with coffee or a snack at a cafe inside the mansion.
Go into Molo Church across the plaza and see the statues of female saints on the pillars and the interior. Be quiet during Mass.
Have lunch at a restaurant around the plaza with a bowl of pancit Molo.
Shop hours may differ, so it is safer to visit before lunch. Wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees when entering the church.

items.title: A heritage day in Iloilo
items.subtitle: From Molo to Jaro and the riverside

children.text: Look around Molo Mansion, Molo Church and the plaza at an easy pace.
Go to Jaro Cathedral in the Jaro district and see its cool interior and bell tower.
Have lunch at a restaurant in central Iloilo and see one or two more heritage buildings in the city.
Go to the Iloilo River Esplanade and walk along the river at sunset.
Return to your lodging after dinner.
Moving between districts takes about
15–30 minutes
by taxi or Grab. Avoid congested hours.
There are direct flights from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO), taking about
1 hour 10 minutes
. Schedules change by season, so check when booking.
The airport is in Santa Barbara, away from central Iloilo City. You get to the city by taxi, Grab or an airport bus or van.
Airport transport options and fares change, so confirm them locally.
The Molo district lies about
3.2 km
east of the city center (City Proper). You can get there by taxi, Grab or jeepney.
Jeepney routes are complicated, so a taxi or Grab is easier the first time. Saying Molo Plaza or Molo Mansion as your destination works.

items.title: Link with the terminal for buses to Antique and the west

children.text: Two guides say buses and vans toward San Jose de Buenavista in southern Antique leave from a terminal in the Molo district (around San Pedro Street), so it is easy to plan a stop at Molo Mansion before heading to Antique. Only one guide lists Molo for Libertad, so confirm the boarding point locally.
The terminal location and timetable can change, so confirm locally before you use it.
Around Molo Plaza, the mansion, the church and the plaza are all within walking distance. At midday when the sun is strong, rest in the shade and walk slowly.
Because the main attractions are indoor shops and cafes, the weather matters little, but for walking around the plaza and church the dry season from November to May is more comfortable.
During the Dinagyang Festival, Iloilo's big event (late January), the city gets crowded and lodging runs short, so book ahead. Around Molo Mansion, family visitors may increase on weekends.

Lodging is plentiful around central Iloilo City, the Esplanade and the Molo district. Molo Mansion is close to the city, so it is easy to reach wherever you stay, and many travelers plan a day each for Jaro, Molo and City Proper. Hotel names and rates change a lot by season, so check recent reviews on a booking site. Molo has a history of Chinese merchants and Spanish families living together, so besides the mansion, the small restaurants and bakeries in the lanes also show the district's past.

The signature food is pancit Molo, named after Molo. Have a bowl around the plaza, and add dessert and coffee at the cafe in the mansion to complete a half-day route. Enjoy the other foods of Iloilo (La Paz batchoy, chicken inasal and more) in other parts of the city. When eating at a stall or market, pick a place whose hygiene you can see for yourself.
The
2026 Molo visitor guide
describes free entry to the mansion garden and ground-floor shop. Ask the operator about upstairs access and special events, and check shop and café hours individually.
When entering the church, wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees, and refrain from taking photos during Mass.
The sun is strong around the plaza at midday, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
Taxi or Grab is convenient for getting around Iloilo, and there is congestion at rush hours.
Souvenirs such as hablon weaving and traditional sweets are priced differently in each shop, so compare two or three.
When taking photos inside the mansion, respect the privacy of customers and staff.
Watch for pickpockets and keep valuables in front of your body.
If your time is short, plan Molo as a one-day trip combined with Jaro Cathedral and the Esplanade.
Around Molo Plaza there are many local families and students, so it is polite not to talk loudly or block the way as a group.

This building is not a museum but a commercial space with souvenir shops and restaurants. The preservation of the interior, the mix of shops and their hours can change often, so check the latest information before you visit.
The garden and ground-floor shop can be visited free of charge during opening hours. Follow staff guidance for upstairs and event spaces.
The shop lineup (Kultura, Sabor Ilonggo, Plantopia and others) may change over time.
Check that the taxi uses a meter, and if a driver demands a flat fare, take another one.
The plaza surface can be slippery on rainy days, so mind your footing.
The plaza may be crowded or closed during church Masses and events.
A Gothic church with red spires across from the mansion, famous for its 16 statues of female saints. It is right on foot.
The cathedral of Iloilo's Jaro district, worth seeing for its bell tower and plaza, reachable by taxi.
A well-kept riverside walkway, pleasant for a walk at sunset.
The central city of Western Visayas, where you can continue your day through museums and food.
A UNESCO World Heritage church southwest of Iloilo that you can link into a day trip.
